_note: What Fallout 4 1.10.163 actually did with this project's scripts on the owner's PC, as reported back (docs/design/VERIFY_LOG.md). tools/papyrus_sim/test_sim.py replays each run in the stand-in engine, with the scripts as they were at that commit, and fails if the stand-in gives a different result. Add a run here only from a real report; never edit a number to make a test pass. From the eleventh run on, a scenario also records the lines the main quest's timing guards wrote to the script log (guard_lines; the report lists them for the whole run, so an empty list is a recorded fact too) and, where a case notes it, whether two handlers overlapped (overlap). A key that begins stand_in_ is not a fact about the game: it tells the replay which of the stand-in's modes to use. Scenario 132 of the eleventh run overlapped in the game, which the stand-in's ordinary mode cannot do at all; it is replayed with every call taking a frame, and the number of tenths waited is then not compared, because that mode provokes overlaps and predicts no timings. A run may carry not_replayed: scenario number, then the key that is not compared, then the reason. It is for lines that came out as they did because of how fast that session of the game happened to run, which the stand-in does not model. The lines themselves are recorded all the same, the replay fails if the stand-in does give them (the exemption is then stale), and everything else about that scenario is compared as usual. From the thirteenth run on a line may also be left out of the replay because it is a place in the game's own test room, which the stand-in does not have; the reason says so. A run may carry scripts_commit: the commit whose scripts are replayed, when that is not the commit the run was made at. It is for a run made on a branch whose commits may not outlive its merge (a merge that squashes or rebases gives them new names): scripts_commit names a commit of the main line that holds the very same scripts, file for file, and the replay checks that they are the same whenever both commits are there.
